description: Let users attach files and images to issue bodies and comments via an upload-then-attach flow, stored on the local filesystem and rendered inline (images) or as downloadable cards (other files) through MarkdownReader.

tasks.title: Backend attachment storage abstraction (local filesystem)
tasks.description: Add IAttachmentStorage + FileSystemAttachmentStorage modeled directly on IWorkflowArtifactStorage, rooted under ~/.mohist/attachments/{projectId}/{attachmentId}/, with server-generated paths, path-traversal guards, atomic .tmp→rename writes, a metadata.json sidecar, and AttachmentStorageOptions (root via Mohist:AttachmentStorage:Root / MOHIST_ATTACHMENT_ROOT, MaxFileBytes, MaxCountPerOwner). The {projectId} path segment enforces project scoping at the storage layer; content and metadata persist across restarts by living on disk.
acceptanceCriteria: IAttachmentStorage exposes path generation, atomic file write, content open, metadata read, and absolute-path resolution mirroring IWorkflowArtifactStorage, but rooted under ~/.mohist/attachments/ with a {projectId}/{attachmentId}/content layout.
WriteFileAsync writes atomically via a temp file plus rename, never overwrites an existing attachment directory, and writes metadata.json alongside the content.
Path traversal attempts (.., absolute/rooted paths, NUL bytes, symlinks) in any storage path are rejected with a clear storage exception.
AttachmentStorageOptions binds Mohist:AttachmentStorage:Root and the MOHIST_ATTACHMENT_ROOT env var, and exposes configurable MaxFileBytes and MaxCountPerOwner with sensible defaults.
Unit tests cover atomic write, the metadata sidecar, traversal rejection, the project-scoped path layout, and the size/count limit primitives, and these tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/server attachment storage module (IAttachmentStorage, FileSystemAttachmentStorage, AttachmentStorageOptions) with passing unit tests
tasks.notes: Reuse the security-hardened shape of IWorkflowArtifactStorage/FileSystemWorkflowArtifactStorage (SanitizeRelativePath, WriteStreamAsync temp+rename, metadata.json) but as a separate interface and root so user content stays isolated from agent-produced artifacts and the object-store backend remains a single-interface swap later.

tasks.title: Backend attachment upload-bind-serve lifecycle and HTTP API
tasks.description: Add the AttachmentRow EF entity plus migration (att_<guid> id, nullable OwnerKind/OwnerId, OriginalFileName, ContentType, Size, StoragePath, ExpiresAt) in the existing SQLite store; an upload service that writes content via IAttachmentStorage and creates a TTL'd pending row (OwnerKind null); bind-at-owning-mutation by extending IssueGrain.AddCommentAsync and the issue-body update to claim attachment ids and clear ExpiresAt; author-initiated removal that deletes stored content, strips att:id references from the owner body, and removes the row; a TTL cleanup job for unbound pending rows; and the HTTP API surface — POST /api/projects/{projectId}/attachments (multipart, size-guarded), GET .../issues/{number}/attachments/{id}/content (and comment-scoped) streaming with Content-Disposition, and DELETE .../attachments/{id}.
acceptanceCriteria: AttachmentRow persists via an EF migration in the existing store; attachments survive a server restart and are scoped to their project (a request from another project is rejected).

POST /attachments accepts a multipart file, enforces MaxFileBytes before fully buffering, writes atomically, and returns a stable att id for an unbound pending row with ExpiresAt set; oversized uploads are rejected with a clear message.
Binding attachment ids through comment create and issue-body update sets OwnerKind+OwnerId and clears ExpiresAt; a bind that would exceed MaxCountPerOwner is rejected with a clear message.

GET content streams via the storage layer, restores the original filename only via Content-Disposition, serves safe image types (png/jpeg/gif/webp) inline and everything else (including SVG) as attachment with a non-executable disposition; the storage path comes only from the id lookup so path traversal is impossible.

Author-initiated removal while the owner is editable deletes stored content, strips every att:id reference to that attachment from the owner body, and removes the row; removal gated out by editability is rejected.
A TTL cleanup job removes unbound pending rows whose ExpiresAt has passed.

Integration/API tests cover upload, bind, serve (inline vs attachment disposition and filename restoration), removal with reference stripping, size/count limit rejections, restart persistence, project scoping, and TTL cleanup, and these tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/server attachment domain model, migration, upload/bind/serve/remove service + HTTP routes, and TTL cleanup with passing integration tests
tasks.notes: Covers REQ-ATT-001, REQ-ATT-002, REQ-ATT-004 (server-side reference strip on removal/bind consistency), REQ-ATT-007, REQ-ATT-008, REQ-ATT-009, REQ-ATT-010. Mirror the serving shape of IssueRoutes.Artifacts.cs (OpenFileContent + Results.Stream) but add Content-Disposition which artifact serving lacks. Treat SVG and any non-allowlist image type as non-image to prevent inline XSS. Bind at the owning mutation (not as a free-standing /attach step) so ownership always matches the persisted markdown body.

tasks.title: Web AttachmentComposer widget (pick/paste/drag, chips, progress)
tasks.description: Build a reusable AttachmentComposer widget that wraps the existing Textarea and accepts files through three input paths — a browse button, clipboard onPaste, and onDrop/onDragOver with a full-card dashed overlay — all routing to the POST /attachments endpoint. It owns per-surface attachment state, renders each file as a chip (image thumbnail for images, colored extension badge otherwise, plus filename, size, and a remove ×), shows a live upload progress bar while in flight, and inserts ![name](att:id) for images / [name](att:id) for non-images at the cursor, stripping the reference when an attachment is removed.
acceptanceCriteria: Browse, paste, and drag-and-drop each upload a file through the same endpoint and return the same stable att id; dragging over the card shows a dashed overlay.
Image chips render a thumbnail; non-image chips render a colored extension badge; both render filename, size, and a remove control.
In-flight attachments render a live progress bar; completed uploads settle into their chip.
Attaching an image inserts ![name](att:id) at the cursor; attaching a non-image inserts [name](att:id); removing an attachment strips its att:id reference from the textarea value.
Component tests cover the three input paths, chip rendering by content type, progress state, and reference insert/strip behavior, and these tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/web shared AttachmentComposer widget with passing component tests
tasks.notes: Covers REQ-ATT-003, REQ-ATT-004 (client-side att:id insert/strip), REQ-ATT-005 (chips, progress, per-surface state). Component tests may mock the upload endpoint. Chip/progress styling should reuse the existing card/pill/blue-accent conventions.

tasks.title: MarkdownReader resolves att:id references (inline image, file card, lightbox)
tasks.description: Add an opt-in resolveAttachment?(id) prop to MarkdownReader. When a resolver is supplied, the image/link component overrides detect att: hrefs: image-typed attachments render inline at their markdown position and open a full-screen lightbox (portal overlay, dark backdrop, click-to-dismiss) on click; non-image attachments render as downloadable file cards showing filename, size, and type; unresolved att: refs render a safe fallback that fetches/executes no untrusted content. When no resolver is supplied, rendering is identical to today so artifact/session/review surfaces are unaffected.
acceptanceCriteria: MarkdownReader accepts an optional resolveAttachment prop; when omitted, rendering is byte-for-byte unchanged (no regression on artifact, session, or review surfaces).
With a resolver, an image att:id reference renders inline at its markdown position (not as a broken link) and opens a dismissible full-screen lightbox on click.
A non-image att:id reference renders as a downloadable file card showing filename, size, and type (not as a plain text link).
An unresolved att:id reference renders a safe fallback and performs no fetch or execution of untrusted content.
Component tests cover inline image rendering, lightbox open/dismiss, file-card rendering, the unresolved fallback, and the no-resolver default path, and these tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/web MarkdownReader opt-in attachment resolver, inline image + file-card overrides, and lightbox with passing component tests
tasks.notes: Implements the MODIFIED REQ-MDR-010 scenarios from specs/markdown-reader/spec.md. Keeping the resolver opt-in is critical: MarkdownReader is shared by artifact, session-transcript, and review surfaces that must not change.

tasks.title: Integrate attachments into the issue body editor and comment composer
tasks.description: Wire AttachmentComposer into the issue body editor (EditIssueDialog) and the IssueDetailPage comment composer, replacing their plain Textareas, and pass a resolveAttachment resolver (backed by the serve endpoint) to the MarkdownReader instances rendering the issue description and each comment. Confirm attachments are authored per-surface and render inline (images, click-to-lightbox) or as file cards (other files) on the real surfaces, and that download preserves the original filename.
acceptanceCriteria: EditIssueDialog's description field and the IssueDetailPage comment box both use AttachmentComposer; browse, paste, and drag-and-drop work on both surfaces.
The issue description MarkdownReader and each comment MarkdownReader receive a resolver and render image attachments inline with a click-to-open lightbox and non-image attachments as file cards.
Downloading a served non-image attachment preserves the original filename.
The issue body composer and each open comment composer maintain independent attachment state; an attachment authored in one surface does not appear in another.

Interaction tests cover attach-via-paste and attach-via-drag on both surfaces, inline render plus lightbox, file-card download with original filename, and per-surface independence, and these tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/web EditIssueDialog and IssueDetailPage wired to AttachmentComposer and a resolving MarkdownReader, with passing interaction tests
tasks.notes: This is the task that makes the feature usable end-to-end on the real authoring surfaces and satisfies the issue's user-facing acceptance criteria. Bind attachment ids via the existing comment-create and issue-body-update calls extended in T-002.
